Triage: lands in `packages/services/service-cluster` (`registerMultiNodeGate` / `allowMultiNode`, verified on `origin/main`) ⇒ `domain:services`, `pm:queue`, type Task. Rationale: implements the maintainer's 2026-08-13 ruling recorded on objectstack-ai/cloud#1275 (refuse excess replicas up to the paid limit, loud warning — NOT whole-cluster degrade); the semantic decision is made, this card is the seam-widening that makes it enforceable, so it does not enter the decision inbox. Contract note for the dispatching seat: `allowMultiNode` is a published seam consumed by `@objectstack/security-enterprise` in the cloud repo — widen it backward-compatibly (count-carrying overload or admitted-count return) and coordinate the one-line consumer change in cloud after this lands (cloud#1291 already computes `{ allowed, refused }`). Size/model suggestion: S–M but with design judgement on the seam shape ⇒ opus.

Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: claude-opus-5`
Serial constraints cleared — no open PR touches `service-cluster`.

## ⛔ The semantic decision is ALREADY RULED — do not re-open it

The maintainer ruled **2026-08-13** (recorded on objectstack-ai/cloud#1275): a licensed `max_nodes` overflow **refuses the excess replicas, runs up to the paid limit, and warns loudly** — explicitly **NOT** whole-cluster degrade.

⚠️ This card is *not* asking whether to do that. It is the seam widening that makes the ruled behaviour **enforceable**: today `allowMultiNode()` returns a bare `{ allowed, reason }`, so the only refusal a license can express through the seam is denying the whole cluster — which is precisely the outcome the ruling rejects. The cap is therefore advisory at the clustering seam, and cloud#1291 shipped everything expressible from the consumer side already.

## ⛔ Backward compatibility is a hard constraint, not a preference

`allowMultiNode` is a **published seam** consumed by `@objectstack/security-enterprise` in the cloud repo. A breaking signature change strands the EE provider. Widen compatibly — a count-carrying overload, an optional argument, or an admitted-count return that still reads correctly for an existing boolean-shaped provider. **Measure what the existing registration sites actually pass and return** before choosing; the card's suggested shape (`allowMultiNode(nodeCount)`) is a suggestion, ⛔ not a ruling.

## The card's own framing of shape is explicitly non-binding

The filer wrote 「Suggested shape (not a decision)」 and is not this repo's triage. Treat both the signature choice and the admitted-count representation as **PM mechanism assumptions open to falsification** — if measurement says a per-node admission callback composes better with how the gate is actually consumed, take that and say why.

## Out of scope

⛔ The one-line cloud consumer change (cloud#1291's `checkNodeCap` already computes `{ allowed, refused }`) is sequenced **after** this lands. Do not open a cloud PR from this card. Report the exact consumer signature this PR leaves behind so the follow-up is mechanical.

## ⛔ CLOSED — but the 2026-08-13 ruling is NOT enforced. Read this before treating it as implemented.

Post-merge inventory, `domain:services` seat #6021, session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`. **PR #8503 MERGED 2026-08-13T16:49:09Z** via the merge queue (25 checks `success`; queue entry confirmed by the `enqueued` event, ⛔ not by the auto-merge receipt, whose fields have come back empty every time this shift). Auto-close verified against `closed_by_pull_requests` → #8503. `pm:dispatched` dropped; nothing is in flight.

⚠️ **This card closing does NOT mean a licensed `max_nodes` cap is enforced. It is not. A cap of 3 with 5 replicas still starts 5.**

I am stating that at the top because this card is exactly the sort that gets read as a checkmark against a maintainer ruling. It is not one.

### What actually changed

The seam can now **express** the ruled verdict: `allowMultiNode(requested?: number)` returns a verdict that may carry `admitted`, and `checkMultiNodeAllowed` totalizes it into `{ allowed, reason, admitted?, refused, capped }`. `capped` marks only a **partial** refusal, so the licensed-overflow case cannot be conflated with the unlicensed one. Backward compatible: the existing EE zero-arg provider keeps working and reads as "no cap".

### ⭐ Why this card's own premise was wrong, recorded so it is not re-derived

This card states the widening is what makes the refusal **binding**, and triage's routing repeated it ("the seam-widening that makes it enforceable"). **Measurement during implementation falsified that.** It is necessary but **not sufficient**, and ⛔ **no consumer-side change can close the gap**:

- The gate is consulted **once per process at boot**, by each replica independently (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:1234-1247`).
- There is **no membership view** — `nodeId` is generated randomly per process (`cluster.ts:123`); nothing registers a node, tracks liveness, or counts live members.
- There is **no ordinal** — `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` is an operator-**declared** desired count, identical in every replica.

With a cap of 3 and 5 replicas, all five compute the **same** verdict and none can determine whether it is one of the admitted 3. The only locally reachable outcomes are "all join" (cap advisory — the status quo) or "all refuse" (the whole-cluster degrade the ruling explicitly rejects). "Run N, refuse N+1" is not producible from a per-replica decision over a count alone.

⭐ The PR therefore **documents the limitation** in the module doc and changeset rather than implying enforcement. That was the right call and it is the reason this closure is safe to make.

### The ruling has three clauses. This card delivered none of them — it delivered the vocabulary.

| Clause (maintainer, 2026-08-13, `objectstack-ai/cloud#1275`) | State | Tracked at |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. Refuse the excess replicas | ⛔ not enforced | **#8501** — needs an atomic slot claim over the `ILock`/`ICounter`/`IKV` primitives this package already ships |
| 2. Run up to the paid limit | ⛔ not enforced | **#8501** (same mechanism) |
| 3. Warn loudly | ⛔ silent | **#8504** — `os serve` calls the gate zero-arg, so the partial-cap state is unreachable from the only call site, not merely unread |

⭐ **#8504 is deliverable now** and does not wait on #8501 — but its wording must be **advisory** while #8501 is open, because a warning that says "2 replicas refused" would be false today.

### For the cloud follow-up

⛔ Not required, and safe to defer: the current zero-arg registration keeps working and reads as uncapped. To adopt the cap, only the registration changes (`maxNodes` is already on the entitlement at `packages/security-enterprise/src/license/entitlement.ts:173,258`) — the exact shape is in PR #8503's body. ⚠️ Adopting it alone still does not enforce anything; it only makes the provider supply the number that #8501 would enforce.

**Anyone auditing "is the 2026-08-13 ruling implemented?" should read #8501 and #8504, not this card.**
